Scope: a passenger station for the SAR railway at Sudair Industrial City (platform, canopy, finishes and station electrical, CCTV and voice evacuation systems) with its access roads RD-01 and RD-02 and their storm water, sewer, potable water, street lighting, telecom and MV/LV networks.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. The 16-Nov-2026 report puts the project at 30.8% against 44.1% planned (SPI 0.70), behind by 13.3%, against 12.4% a week earlier. The P6 update of the same date forecasts completion on 22-Dec-2027, 138 days after the contract date and one week later than last week.

P6 now finishes the project 138 days after the contract date. The 16-Nov-2026 P6 update moves the project finish from 15-Dec-2027 to 22-Dec-2027 (total float −119 days). The logic and durations are unchanged from last week: the MV design approvals that start the driving path have still not started, so the engineering phase finish moved from 21-Nov-2026 to 28-Nov-2026 and every later milestone moved by the same week. The station excavation now starts on 29-Nov-2026. This week earned 0.91% against 1.86% planned, half the plan and below the 1.87% a week now needed to finish on 06-Aug-2027. Procurement earned nothing for a second week and stays at 25.3% against 85.9% planned; the station package has not started.

P6 misses the contract finish by 138 days, while the weekly report still forecasts 06-Aug-2027. Every open P6 milestone moved by one week since the 09-Nov-2026 update: project finish to 22-Dec-2027, finishing works to 12-Dec-2027, MV works to 25-Aug-2027 with −90 days of float (against 05-May-2027 in the weekly report) and road and paving works to 01-Mar-2027 with −61 days (against 31-Dec-2026). The engineering phase, forecast for 21-Sep-2026 in the weekly report, now ends on 28-Nov-2026, because the two MV design approvals (11 working days each) have not started. Site and platform works still show 11 days of float on 11-Jul-2027, although the station works before them carry −119 days and platform work waits for the SAR fence permission.

Procurement of key materials

Share of the required quantity delivered, from the Completion Rate column. Source: Procurement sheet, weekly report 16-Nov-2026, unchanged since 26-Oct-2026.

Eight long-lead items not yet submittedMetal railing, canopy, MV duct banks, MV cables, substations, lighting poles, street-lighting luminaires and outdoor lighting fixtures are all still marked "Not submitted". The required PO dates for the railing (25-Aug-2026), the MV duct banks and cables (12-Oct-2026), the substations (19-Oct-2026) and the street-lighting luminaires (10-Nov-2026) have passed; those for the canopy (19-Nov-2026) and outdoor fixtures (23-Nov-2026) fall within a week. The look-ahead plan schedules the MV duct bank, MV cable and substation submissions for 17 to 24-Nov-2026.
Deliveries on the critical pathIn the 16-Nov-2026 P6 the kerbstone delivery has −58 days of float, the asphalt delivery −67 days and the canopy delivery −45 days, each seven days worse than last week. Interlock, waterproofing, the LV distribution panel, street-lighting feeder panels, CCTV, voice evacuation, manhole covers and valves have no delivery figure yet. The summary still counts 22 of 27 purchase orders issued.

Data notes

  • The weekly report gives no week number on its cover; its Milestones sheet states “Current Contract Weeks: 32 of 69”, which this report uses. Whole weeks from site handover (07-Apr-2026) to the data date give 31, because contract weeks count from 1.
  • The previous-week column restates 09-Nov-2026 at 197,128 earned man-hours (construction 122,598), against 197,134 (construction 122,604) in last week's report. The week's gain of 6,023 man-hours (0.91%) is the report's own figure; the difference between the two cumulative totals is 6,017.
  • P6 labour units give 202,223 of 659,805 man-hours (30.7%), 928 below the weekly report's 203,151 (30.8%). Last week the two matched.
  • Procurement earned man-hours stay at 23,398 for a second week, while its planned figure rose from 76,904 to 79,373 (85.9%).
  • Major Quantities: subgrade reads 19,000 m³ while two helper columns still show 18,182.25 and 3,182.25 m³; aggregate base course helper columns still show 9,875.94 and 21,459.19. Curbstone rose to 3,000 m² with no curbstone installation started in P6, and is in m² there but in m on the Procurement sheet, which gives kerbstone a completion rate of 1.4 (140%). The asphalt total is 13,360 m³ there but 3,420 m³ on the Procurement sheet.
  • The cover sheet's headline “Earn Value” and its SPI are cost-based (BOQ value), not physical progress, and are not used in this report.
  • The weekly report gives forecast completion 06-Aug-2027 with zero variance, while the P6 update of the same date finishes on 22-Dec-2027. The cover sheet still gives “Revised Completion” as 07-Apr-2026, the site handover date.
  • MV works baseline: 12-May-2027 in the Milestones sheet's baseline column but 22-May-2027 on the cover sheet and in its “Latest” column.
  • The FIR summary now lists FIRs up to FIR-0198 (11-Nov-2026) with their BOQ descriptions filled in, while the FIR count is 202.
  • Manpower: the weekly summary gives 87 (65 manual, 22 non-manual), but the trade breakdown totals 86 (engineers 10 to 9). The monthly histogram's November column still repeats October, and the October plan is 217 there but 60 in the weekly summary panel.
  • Schedule sheet: 424 critical-path activities this week against 185 “last week”, although last week's sheet gave 488.
  • The P6 file is now named project “SUD1-05-018-NEW - B1-2” (last week B1-9). Against last week's file it has the same 855 activities, relationships and durations; 31 activities were completed and 9 started. Three completed GRP pipe activities had their actual finishes moved from 07–08-Nov-2026 back to 11–13-Oct-2026. No actual date falls after the data date.
  • P6 logic to check: site and platform works show +11 days of float although the station works before them carry −119 days; and there are two finish milestones, Project Finish on 22-Dec-2027 and Project Finish Milestone on 19-Dec-2027.
  • The HSE inspection sheet and the FIR summary still carry project ID SUD1-02-011, and the Conclusion sheet describes a different project. The risk register still describes the project as ahead of schedule, and risks 3120-4 and 3120-5 are marked Open in one column and Close in another.
